bib.title: GNN-RAG: Graph Neural Retrieval for Large Language Model Reasoning

question: Can a GNN used as retriever over a dense KG subgraph, with a fine-tuned LLM as reader, beat LLM-based retrieval on multi-hop KGQA?
hypothesis: GNNs handle complex multi-hop graph structure better than LLMs, so GNN retrieval plus LLM reasoning outperforms LLM-based retrieval, and combining both retrievers adds further gains.
contributions: Framework: GNN-RAG repurposes GNNs for KGQA retrieval to enhance the reasoning abilities of LLMs
Effectiveness & Faithfulness: state-of-the-art on WebQSP and CWQ; retrieves multi-hop information
Efficiency: improves vanilla LLMs without additional LLM calls; outperforms or matches GPT-4 with a 7B tuned LLM

method.summary: A GNN (ReaRev) scores all nodes in a PageRank-Nibble dense subgraph (top 2,000 entities) as answer vs non-answer; nodes up to cumulative softmax probability 0.95 are candidates, and shortest paths from question entities to them (NetworkX) are verbalised and fed to a LLaMA2-Chat-7B fine-tuned (RoG recipe) on the benchmark training sets. Retrieval augmentation (RA) takes the union of GNN paths and RoG LLM-generated relation paths.
method.task: knowledge graph question answering (KGQA), weakly supervised (question-answer pairs only)

datasets.name: WebQSP
datasets.preprocessing: dense subgraph by PageRank Nibble from linked entities, top m=2,000 entities (He et al. 2021); avg |Vq| 1,429.8; answer coverage 94.9%

datasets.name: CWQ (Complex WebQuestions 1.1)
datasets.preprocessing: same KG as WebQSP; avg |Vq| 1,305.8; answer coverage 79.3%; up to 4 hops; composition 45%, conjunction 45%, comparative 5%, superlative 5%

datasets.name: MetaQA-3
datasets.size: more than 100k 3-hop questions; KG about 43k entities, 135k triples
datasets.split: 114,196 train / 14,274 dev / 14,274 test; only 1,000 (1%) training questions used
datasets.source: Zhang et al. 2018 / WikiMovies Miller et al. 2016

models.name: ReaRev (GNN retriever, +SBERT default, +LMSR)
models.architecture: question-conditioned GNN, sum aggregation, L layers; relation matching w(q,r)=phi(q(k) * r) with pretrained LM encoder
models.init_from: SBERT (Reimers and Gurevych 2019) or LMSR (Zhang et al. 2022a) as LM in Eq 3
models.layers: deep L=3 in Table 1 analysis; the ReaRev layer count is not stated

other.note: suggested hyperparameters of official ReaRev code used; no hyperparameter search

other.fine_tuned_on: training question-answer pairs, with shortest paths from question entities to answers as input (RoG recipe)

models.name: RoG
models.architecture: LLaMA2-Chat-7B fine-tuned to generate relation paths, beam search k (3 or 4 calls)

other.use: plug-in readers in Table 5; ChatGPT accessed via API as of May 2024

training.objective: GNN: node classification answers vs non-answers (softmax over subgraph nodes); LLM: instruction fine-tuning to output list of answers given reasoning paths
training.hardware: GNNs: one Nvidia GeForce RTX-3090, 128GB RAM; LLMs: 4 A100 GPUs with NVLink, 512GB memory

other.hyperparameters: 'we use their suggested hyperparameters, without performing further hyperparameter search' (ReaRev and RoG code)
other.training_data: retriever and reader trained on WebQSP+CWQ per Table 14 (GNN-RAG retriever on a single dataset)

inference.decoding: GNN: top nodes by sorted probability with cumulative probability threshold; LLM reader decoding not stated
inference.samples: not stated; tables give single values, no seeds or variance
inference.prompting: fine-tuned reader prompt with verbalised reasoning paths 'q entity -> relation -> entity ... -> answer entity'
inference.retrieval: PageRank-Nibble subgraph m=2,000; GNN answer candidates; NetworkX shortest paths from question entities; RA = union with RoG paths

parameters.rog_beams_k: 3 (4 total calls incl. reader; Table 6 compares 1 vs 3)

metrics.name: Hit
metrics.definition: whether any true answer is found in the generated response

metrics.name: H@1
metrics.definition: accuracy of the top/first predicted answer

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: harmonic balance of recall (true answers found) and precision (false answers found) of generated answers

metrics.name: Answer Coverage
metrics.definition: whether retriever fetches at least one correct answer

metrics.name: #Input Tokens
metrics.definition: median number of input tokens of retrieved KG paths

eval.protocol: single run per configuration as printed; no seeds, variance or significance test reported; semantic-parsing methods excluded because they need SPARQL annotations; most baseline numbers quoted from prior papers

availability.data: KGQA results provided at the same repo; datasets public

prompts.text:
Please generate a valid relation path that can be helpful for answering the following question:
{Question}

Based on the reasoning paths, please answer the given question. Please keep the answer as simple as possible and return all the possible answers as a list.\n Reasoning Paths: {Reasoning Paths} \n Question: {Question}

Based on the provided knowledge, please answer the given question. Please keep the answer as simple as possible and return all the possible answers as a list.\n Knowledge: {Reasoning Paths} \n Question: {Question}

Your tasks is to use the following facts and answer the question. Make sure that you use the information from the facts provided. Please keep the answer as simple as possible and return all the possible answers as a list.\n The facts are the following: {Reasoning Paths} \n Question: {Question}

limits: GNN-RAG assumes the subgraph contains answer nodes; CWQ subgraphs contain an answer in only 79.3% of questions (App E).
Shortest-path extraction returns empty paths if the KG has disconnected parts (App D.7, E).
GNNs are weak on simple 1-hop questions needing semantic matching (Theorem A.3, Table 8); LLM retriever better there.
Weak GNNs (NSM, GraftNet) are not effective retrievers (Table 10).
No seeds, variance or significance tests; no optimizer, learning rate, batch size or epochs reported (defers to ReaRev and RoG code).
Baseline numbers (ToG etc.) are quoted from other papers, so setups may differ; the ToG+GPT-4 cost is an unexplained estimate.
Reader is fine-tuned on WebQSP+CWQ training data, whereas ToG is prompt-only.
Theorem B.3 is shown for a binary relevance function w, a simplification of the learned w.
